messages:
maria: Customer hit intermittent 500s in the Console when switching orgs. They can reproduce within ~30s. Asking for concise repro steps we can send them (HAR + console logs + an easy curl replay). Please include where to find the request-id in the response headers. @support-bot can you also remind them to attach the account/org id and local time?

alex: Short, copy-pasteable instructions I send: 1) Open Chrome DevTools (F12) -> Network tab -> check "Preserve log". 2) Click Console -> check "Preserve log" as well. 3) Reproduce the issue. 4) In Network: right-click any request -> "Save all as HAR with content". 5) In Console: right-click -> "Save as..." to get a text dump. 6) Screenshot the failing network row and open the response headers to show `x-request-id` (or `X-Request-Id`) and the response body. 7) Attach HAR + console log + screenshot + the exact local time. :thumbsup:

alex: Also ask them to include: browser/version (Chrome 1xx), OS, account email, org id, and the sequence of clicks that fail.

jordan: Example curl they can run (replace placeholders):
```bash
TOKEN=REPLACE_WITH_TOKEN
# simple replay of the failing API path (include the same path + query from the Network trace)
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Replay-From-Browser: 1" \n  -d '{"prompt":"test"}' \\n  "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate"
```
Note: if the console/network shows a `Set-Cookie` or a cookie-based session, include the cookie header from the request: `-H "Cookie: ${COOKIE}"`.

jordan: If they can capture the `x-request-id` from the response headers (Network -> Headers -> Response Headers) please paste that id in the support ticket. Example header we look for: `x-request-id: 01H3KZJ5-abc123` — with that we can grep logs and attach a trace.

support-bot: Quick checklist to paste to customer: 
• Chrome (or record browser + version)
• Steps to reproduce (exact clicks)
• HAR file (Network -> Save all as HAR with content)
• Console log (Console -> right click -> Save as...)
• Screenshot of failing row + response headers (show `x-request-id`)
• Local time of repro (UTC if possible)
• Account email / org id

eng-oncall: When you have the `x-request-id` and the UTC timestamp we will: 1) grep API logs for that request id; 2) look at backend traces and ingress logs; 3) confirm whether it's 5xx from our service or an upstream dependency; 4) share a short timeline. If they can't get a request-id, ask them to reproduce while you watch (screenshare) or use a curl we provide so the request is created with a header we can correlate (`X-Client-Request-ID: <value>`).

maria: Thanks all — sending these steps to the customer now. I'll ask them to upload the HAR + console log to the ticket (or to the secure upload link) and to paste back the `x-request-id` if present. Will update once they reply. :white_check_mark:
